issues.description: PersonResource constructor signature in the solution does not match the intended design: the template and problem expect PersonResource to be constructed with a PersonService, but the solution's PersonResource constructor takes a String. This creates a structural mismatch (and a compile error) that contradicts the layered design described in the problem statement and shown in the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the solution's PersonResource to accept a PersonService (public PersonResource(PersonService personService)) and assign it to the personService field. This restores consistency with the template and the described web/application/service layering.

issues.description: The PersonResource constructor in the solution repository accepts a parameter typed as String named 'personService', whereas the template and the problem statement describe/inject a PersonService. This mismatch (using String instead of PersonService) breaks the conceptual mapping between the Web layer (PersonResource) and the Application layer (PersonService) and will confuse students comparing template, problem description, and solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution repository, change the PersonResource constructor parameter type from String to PersonService (e.g., public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }) so it matches the template and the problem statement's description of the web layer injecting PersonService.
